169:1: If God is seeking us even while we seek him, how does that Father become visible in the life of Jesus?

170:1: Where is the kingdom of heaven that Jesus proclaimed, and why does it begin within us rather than in a distant future or a visible church?
170:4: In Paper 169 we saw the parables and the teaching about the Father that Jesus gave during his last week at Pella. Paper 170 now takes up the final sermon he preached at Pella on the afternoon of Saturday, March 11. It was one of the outstanding addresses of his public ministry, a comprehensive and complete discussion of the kingdom of heaven (170:0.1).
170:5: Jesus used "the kingdom of heaven" and "the kingdom of God" as meaning the same thing. But the idea of awaiting a temporal king was so deeply rooted in the Jewish mind that even the apostles were confused about its meaning (170:0.1). The book adds to this sermon remarks made at other times and words spoken to the apostles that evening, and it also comments on how the concept of the kingdom later changed within the church (170:0.2).
170:6: So where, after all, is the kingdom of heaven that Jesus spoke of, and why does it begin within us rather than in a distant future or a visible organization?

170:12: In Jesus' day many ideas about the kingdom were mixed together. The prophets of the Hebrew scriptures spoke of the kingdom both as a present reality and as a future hope to come with the Messiah. To these were added the later Jewish idea of a supernatural kingdom and the Persian teaching that good would triumph over evil at the end of the world (170:1.1-1.6). Jesus chose to use the term kingdom of heaven, taking up the most essential heritage of both Judaism and the Persian religion (170:1.7).
